Good enough, with nothing to be ashamed of. You're waving something through: not impressive, but it would hold up if anyone asked.
To chase after gain or comfort, a little shamefully. You hear 贪, greed, in it, so 贪图便宜 or 贪图享乐 always comes with a raised eyebrow.
Easy to get along with, someone who doesn't fuss or insist. It's real praise in Chinese social life, where you value a person who goes along without friction.
The key people who hold a team up. When your boss calls you 业务骨干, you're being praised, and you also know more work is on its way.
Hard to please, as if you were waiting on a demanding master. You hear 伺候, to wait on someone, so you say it with an eye roll about a client, a boss or a picky baby.

gloss: to join one's husband's household upon marriage
note: A bride coming to live in her husband's family. You hear the old order of things in 新媳妇进门, with a mother-in-law waiting on the other side of the door.

gloss: (used to humorously or indirectly refer to sth embarrassing, funny etc, or when one can't think of the right word)
note: A coy stand-in for something you'd rather not say. When you say 你这样有点那个, you trail off and trust the listener to fill in the awkward word.
